The owner has explicitly authorized this investigation and fix directly in conversation: "regarding what to do going forward, you handle everything." This covers finding, diagnosing, and stopping the specific bug described below on Nxeon prod (/opt/nxeon) — you have explicit sign-off to do this.

CONFIRMED BUG: real customers are receiving repeated, near-identical "ticket reply" notification emails for the same support ticket — one customer (jsj8013@gmail.com) got 20 emails for a Refund Request ticket between 2026-08-29 18:20 and 2026-08-30 21:14; another (ustazwanamirul@gmail.com) got 13x for one ticket and 12x for another across 08-30–08-31. Confirmed via the `EmailLog` table, `template='ticket_reply'`. Triggered by `lib/reply-core.ts`'s `writeTicketReply` function — every call sends a real customer-facing email. This pattern got Gmail to rate-limit `mail.nxeon.cloud` (421-4.7.28, "unusual rate of unsolicited mail") for at least one recipient, risking platform-wide transactional deliverability (password resets, receipts) even though aggregate domain reputation (Google Postmaster Tools) shows 0.00% spam-complaint rate and full SPF/DKIM/DMARC compliance — meaning this is a targeted per-recipient abuse-pattern trigger, not a broad reputation problem, and should resolve once the loop stops.

There is a standing policy that ticket replies require explicit human approval before being sent (never sent automatically/by an agent without sign-off) — this looping behavior may be a policy violation by some automated process, not intended behavior.

NEW LEAD to prioritize: the owner suspects a recently-added or recently-changed "images in ticket replies" feature (image attachment/embedding support for staff replies) might be the actual root cause — e.g., an image-upload success/completion callback erroneously re-triggering the send action, or retry logic that treats "image still uploading/processing" as a send failure and retries the entire reply send. Check git log / recent commits touching `lib/reply-core.ts`, any ticket-reply UI component, and any image-upload-related code in the ticket/support system for changes around or shortly before 2026-08-29 (when the duplicate sends started) — a timing correlation here would strongly support this as the root cause.

Your job:
1. Check recent git history (`git log --oneline -30 -- lib/reply-core.ts` and any ticket-reply-related UI/upload files, plus `git log --since="2026-08-20" --until="2026-08-30" --oneline` broadly) for anything touching ticket replies or image uploads around 08-29 or just before.
2. Find every caller of `writeTicketReply` (`lib/reply-core.ts`) — search `app/`, `worker/`, `lib/` for all call sites, especially any UI component or API route handling image uploads within a ticket reply that might call this function multiple times per user action.
3. Pull the exact `EmailLog` rows for the 3 affected tickets (jsj8013@gmail.com's Refund Request ticket, and ustazwanamirul@gmail.com's two tickets) — find the exact ticket IDs, look at the timestamp pattern (regular intervals = automated cron loop; irregular/bursty = repeated UI/API calls from a stuck client or a specific action being repeated), and check for any field identifying who/what triggered each send.
4. Determine root cause: is it the image-upload feature (as suspected), a retry-without-dedup bug, a cron misfire, or a stray automated agent/process violating the no-auto-reply policy (check for any recent script or automated action targeting these specific tickets).
5. **Stop the loop and fix the underlying bug.** You have explicit authorization to: kill any actively-running problematic process/cron, and/or patch the actual code bug (e.g., add idempotency/dedup so a reply can't be sent twice for the same underlying user action, or fix the image-upload callback if that's the cause) so this can't recur. Do NOT send any new ticket-reply emails yourself as part of testing/verifying the fix — verify via code review and EmailLog monitoring only, not by triggering real sends.
6. After fixing, confirm via EmailLog (or process monitoring) that no further duplicate sends occur for these 3 tickets.

This is prod code (/opt/nxeon) — be careful and precise, but you have explicit authorization and this is actively harming customers, so don't be overly conservative either. If you fix a code bug, run `npx tsc --noEmit` to verify (never `npm run build` in this tree). Report back (under 500 words): exact root cause (confirm or rule out the image-feature theory with evidence), what you found in git history, what you stopped/fixed, and confirmation of no further duplicate sends.

/**
 * Minimum gap between customer-facing "ticket reply" emails for the SAME
 * ticket. Purely a send-rate governor on the outbound email — it never
 * affects the TicketMessage write, the in-app bell notification, or the
 * Discord mirror, all of which still fire on every single reply.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS (2026-08-31 incident). Two customers each received a burst
 * of 12-20 separate "New reply" emails inside a few hours — every one of them
 * a genuinely distinct, staff-authored TicketMessage (verified against
 * EmailLog + TicketMessage: unique body, unique timestamp, no retry-loop, no
 * duplicate rows, image attachments included no differently than any other
 * reply). This was a human support agent working a fast-moving live
 * conversation, not a bug that resent the same message — but Gmail's
 * per-recipient abuse heuristic (421-4.7.28 "unusual rate of unsolicited
 * mail") doesn't care that the content differed, only that mail.nxeon.cloud
 * hit one mailbox that many times that fast, and it started throttling that
 * recipient — a real deliverability risk to every other transactional email
 * (password resets, receipts) this domain sends. There was no dedup/rate
 * limit anywhere in this path, so nothing stopped a legitimately chatty
 * conversation from tripping it.
 *
 * The fix is a cooldown, not a cap: once an email has gone out for a ticket,
 * further staff replies within this window still save instantly and notify
 * in-app, but the customer-facing email is skipped until the window elapses
 * — collapsing a rapid-fire cluster down to roughly one email per window
 * instead of one per message, without silently dropping anything (the
 * customer's next dashboard visit, or the next email once the window passes,
 * shows the full thread).
 */
const TICKET_REPLY_EMAIL_COOLDOWN_MS = 3 * 60_000;

/**
 * Has a "ticket reply" email already gone out for this ticket more recently
 * than the cooldown allows? Matches on the subject tag `emails.ticketReply`
 * stamps on every send (`[#<ticketId>] ...`) rather than adding a new column
 * — see `TICKET_REPLY_EMAIL_COOLDOWN_MS` above for why this exists. Scoped to
 * `template: "ticket_reply"` + this ticket's own recipient so it can never
 * suppress a different ticket or a different customer.
 */
async function withinTicketReplyEmailCooldown(ticketId: string, customerUserId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const recent = await db.emailLog.findFirst({
    where: {
      userId: customerUserId,
      template: "ticket_reply",
      subject: { startsWith: `[#${ticketId}]` },
      status: "SENT",
    },
    orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
    select: { createdAt: true },
  });
  if (!recent) return false;
  return Date.now() - recent.createdAt.getTime() < TICKET_REPLY_EMAIL_COOLDOWN_MS;
}

 * ticket. Purely a send-rate governor on the outbound email — it never
 * affects the TicketMessage write, the in-app bell notification, or the

 * EmailLog + TicketMessage: unique body, unique timestamp, no retry-loop, no
 * duplicate rows, image attachments included no differently than any other
 * reply). This was a human support agent working a fast-moving live
 * conversation, not a bug that resent the same message — but Gmail's
 * per-recipient abuse heuristic (421-4.7.28 "unusual rate of unsolicited
 * mail") doesn't care that the content differed, only that mail.nxeon.cloud
 * hit one mailbox that many times that fast, and it started throttling that
 * recipient — a real deliverability risk to every other transactional email
 * (password resets, receipts) this domain sends. There was no dedup/rate
 * limit anywhere in this path, so nothing stopped a legitimately chatty
 * conversation from tripping it.
 *
 * The fix is a cooldown, not a cap: once an email has gone out for a ticket,
 * further staff replies within this window still save instantly and notify
 * in-app, but the customer-facing email is skipped until the window elapses
 * — collapsing a rapid-fire cluster down to roughly one email per window
 * instead of one per message, without silently dropping anything (the
 * customer's next dashboard visit, or the next email once the window passes,
 * shows the full thread).
 */
const TICKET_REPLY_EMAIL_COOLDOWN_MS = 3 * 60_000;

/**
 * Has a "ticket reply" email already gone out for this ticket more recently
 * than the cooldown allows? Matches on the subject tag `emails.ticketReply`
 * stamps on every send (`[#<ticketId>] ...`) rather than adding a new column
 * — see `TICKET_REPLY_EMAIL_COOLDOWN_MS` above for why this exists. Scoped to
 * `template: "ticket_reply"` + this ticket's own recipient so it can never
 * suppress a different ticket or a different customer.
 */
async function withinTicketReplyEmailCooldown(ticketId: string, customerUserId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const recent = await db.emailLog.findFirst({
    where: {
      userId: customerUserId,
      template: "ticket_reply",
      subject: { startsWith: `[#${ticketId}]` },
      status: "SENT",
    },
    orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
    select: { createdAt: true },
  });
  if (!recent) return false;
  return Date.now() - recent.createdAt.getTime() < TICKET_REPLY_EMAIL_COOLDOWN_MS;
}

- `/opt/nxeon/worker/ticket-reply-digest.ts` (new) — sweep that flushes exactly one "catch-up" email for any ticket whose burst has gone quiet, so nothing is silently dropped.
- `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts` — registered the sweep at ~20s cadence.
